en.title: Blade Runner 2099 Trailer: Humans Fight Replicant Rule This Thanksgiving
en.summary: The final trailer for Prime Video's **Blade Runner 2099** has landed, showcasing a grim Los Angeles where replicants reign supreme and humanity struggles for survival. The limited series, set to premiere this Thanksgiving, pits a fugitive human against her programmed destiny.
en.body:
The veil has lifted on **Blade Runner 2099**, with Prime Video dropping the final trailer for the highly anticipated limited series. Set to debut this Thanksgiving, the footage plunges viewers into a dystopian Los Angeles fifty years after the events of **Blade Runner 2049**, where the roles have dramatically reversed. Replicants are now in control, and humans find themselves relegated to menial roles, living at the mercy of their own creations.

The trailer centers on **Cora**, played by **Hunter Schafer**, a human on the run who assumes the identity of a Blade Runner to infiltrate the ruling class. Her mission forces her into an uneasy alliance with **Olwen**, a replicant portrayed by the legendary **Michelle Yeoh**, who is facing the end of her programmed lifespan. The narrative hints at a desperate struggle for humanity's future, with Cora tasked with uncovering a truth that could destabilize the fragile new world order.

> "The old world forever fights to come back. Humans want what was taken from them. But it’s our time now." — **Olwen**

This quote from **Olwen** underscores the central conflict: a war not just for dominance, but for the very definition of life and legacy. The replicants, having achieved their autonomy, now grapple with their own existential questions, mirroring the very struggles of the humans they replaced. The series seems poised to explore whether humanity, in its desperation, truly deserves the salvation it seeks, and if the replicants, in their ascendancy, have found a new purpose beyond their original programming.

## The Replicant Reckoning

The trailer teases a profound identity crisis among the replicants themselves. Having achieved victory, they are now questioning their existence: do they aspire to be more human, to transcend humanity, or to attain a godlike status? This internal conflict adds a rich layer to the external war. The visual landscape of Los Angeles, reimagined and seemingly reborn under replicant rule, promises a stunning, yet unsettling, backdrop for this complex narrative. The series directly confronts the legacy of **Rick Deckard** and **K**, pushing the boundaries of what it means to be alive in this meticulously crafted universe.

## What Fans Can Expect

Fans of the **Blade Runner** saga can anticipate a continuation of the franchise's signature philosophical depth and atmospheric world-building. The pairing of **Hunter Schafer** and **Michelle Yeoh** offers a compelling dynamic, hinting at complex character arcs and a nuanced exploration of the human-replicant divide. The stakes are incredibly high, with the fate of both species hanging in the balance. The trailer effectively builds anticipation for a story that will likely challenge viewers' perceptions of identity, memory, and survival.

## What's Next

**Blade Runner 2099** is scheduled to premiere on Prime Video on November 25, 2026. Viewers can expect a gripping narrative that expands the iconic **Blade Runner** universe, offering new insights into the enduring questions of artificial intelligence and the human condition.

By Vanessa Armstrong | Published on November 9, 2026 Photo: Clay Enos/Prime Video Comment 0 Share New Share Blade Runner 2099 Trailer Sees Humans Trying to Fell the Replicant Regime&url= target=”_blank” title=”Twitter”> Blade Runner 2099 Trailer Sees Humans Trying to Fell the Replicant Regime” target=”_blank” title=”Pinterest”> Photo: Clay Enos/Prime Video We’ve got the final trailer for Blade Runner 2099 , the limited series coming to Prime Video this Thanksgiving, and in it we see the human Cora (Hunter Schafer) trying to overturn the replicant uprising from the inside. This trailer does an excellent job of setting the stakes. It’s Los Angeles, 2099, and the replicants are now in charge, with humans now in menial roles and at the mercy of the beings they created. Many humans are, unsurprisingly, not happy about that. And Cora is now pretending to be a replicant Blade Runner who needs to get close to her new replicant partner, Olwen (Michelle Yeoh), for reasons that are only teased at in the video. The official synopsis gives us a bit more to go on: Fifty years after the events of Blade Runner 2049 , Los Angeles has been reborn, just not by humanity. Cora, a fugitive in a final bid to stop running, takes on one last identity: a Blade Runner. Forced to partner with Olwen, a Replicant days from dying, she hunts down a runaway hiding a truth that could collapse a fragile city. In addition to Yoeh and Schafer, the show stars Dimitri Abold ( The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes ), Lewis Gribben ( Somewhere Boy ), Katelyn Rose Downey ( The Nun II ), Daniel Rigby ( Renegade Nell ), Johnny Harris ( A Gentleman in Moscow ), Amy Lennox ( Only Child ), Sheila Atim ( The Woman King ), Matthew Needham ( House of the Dragon ), Tom Burke ( Furiosa ), and Maurizio Lombardi ( Ripley ). The limited series comes from showrunner Silka Luisa ( Halo, Shining Girls ) and is executive produced by Ridley Scott. All eight episodes of Blade Runner 2099 will be available to stream on Prime Video on November 25, 2026. Happy Thanksgiving!
